The number of stars as a function of parallax \( p \) is given by \( N(p) \propto 1/p^5 \). Parallax is inversely proportional to distance: \( p \propto 1/r \), so \( p = k/r \) for some constant \( k \). The differential number of stars in a parallax interval \( dp \) is \( dN \propto (1/p^5) \, dp \). Substituting \( p = k/r \) and \( dp = -k/r^2 \, dr \), the number of stars in a distance interval \( dr \) is \( dN \propto (r^5/k^5) \cdot (k/r^2) \, dr = (r^3/k^4) \, dr \). Thus, the number of stars per unit range of distance scales as \( r^3 \).

Answer: A
